rules.text: At current UTS compatibility: omitted partition specification or MAXPARTITIONS selects PBG; NUMPARTS without MAXPARTITIONS selects PBR; both select PBG with an initial partition count.
At APPLCOMPAT V12R1M504 or later, new base table spaces are PBG/PBR UTS and new tables cannot be created in existing non-UTS spaces.
Initial PBG NUMPARTS cannot exceed MAXPARTITIONS.
PBG data sets must be Db2-managed; USING VCAT is invalid.
A table in PBG can have only nonpartitioned indexes.
PBR RPN supports 1-1024 G integer DSSIZE and up to 4096 partitions, with required extended-format/addressability support.
PAGENUM ABSOLUTE is deprecated and uses page-size/DSSIZE-dependent partition ceilings; retain it only for compatibility coverage.
Partition-level values override table-space-level values, which override database or subsystem defaults.
Explicit PCTFREE plus FOR UPDATE cannot exceed 99; -1 requests automatic update reservation behavior.
LOCKSIZE TABLESPACE requires LOCKMAX omitted or zero; omitted LOCKMAX otherwise depends on LOCKSIZE.
GBPCACHE SYSTEM is a LOB setting and must not be generated for an ordinary base table space.
Work-file table spaces are PBG, use fixed work-file behaviors, and reject the ordinary clauses listed in the table-space chapter.
FOR SORT and FOR DGTT are mutually exclusive.
LOB spaces use CREATE LOB TABLESPACE, support auxiliary-table data rather than base rows, and accept only LOCKSIZE ANY or LOB; TABLESPACE, PAGE, and ROW are invalid in this form.
These physical attributes can appear on CREATE TABLE only when Db2 implicitly creates its base table space; an explicit table-space target rejects them.
Compare SYSTABLESPACE and every ordered SYSTABLEPART row; parent-only comparison misses partition overrides.

rules.text: Explicit elements, LIKE, AS-result WITH NO DATA, and MQT are alternative definition families rather than combinable fragments.
The top-level repeat path permits accepted clause permutations, but the same top-level clause must not be specified more than once.

EXCLUDING COLUMN DEFAULTS, INCLUDING COLUMN DEFAULTS, and USING TYPE DEFAULTS are AS-result/fullselect choices and must not be specified with LIKE; LIKE supports the documented identity, row-change-timestamp, and EXCLUDING XML TYPE MODIFIERS choices.
Applicable copy-option clauses can appear in accepted permutations, each option can be specified at most once, and the three column-default choices are mutually exclusive.
MQT refresh-option clauses can appear in accepted permutations, but each option can be specified at most once.
Ordinary columns require a type; omission is limited to generated timestamp forms for which IBM defines an implicit type.
Eligible column clauses follow the diagram's repeat path and can appear in supported permutations, but the same specific column clause or constraint form must not be specified more than once.

ALWAYS is optional and is the default after GENERATED. BY DEFAULT is an alternative only for identity, eligible ROWID, and row-change-timestamp forms; ROWID is the column data type before GENERATED, not a token after it.
Identity options can appear in accepted permutations and can be separated by optional commas; an identity option must not be specified more than once.
An XML type modifier contains one or more comma-separated XMLSCHEMA specifications selected by ID or URI/NO NAMESPACE with optional LOCATION, followed by an optional global ELEMENT.

A non-deterministic generated-expression column must not specify CCSID 1200, CCSID 1208, or FIELDPROC and is limited to the enumerated operation, special-register, and package-session-variable sources.
Identity, ROWID, temporal timestamp, row-change, transaction-start, and XML columns reject an ordinary DEFAULT clause as documented.
A table can have only one identity column and its type must be exact numeric with scale zero.
Every primary-key column must be NOT NULL and the table can have at most one primary key.

Primary/unique keys and eligible BY DEFAULT ROWID need matching ordinary UNIQUE enforcing indexes; explicit-space dynamic SQL can leave the table incomplete until they exist, while eligible implicit/schema-processor paths can create them.
An omitted delete rule resolves to RESTRICT under Db2 rules and NO ACTION under standard rules; record CURRENT RULES.
ON DELETE SET NULL requires at least one nullable foreign-key column.
CHECK uses the IBM-listed restricted condition language and is not an arbitrary SQL search condition; its text limit is 3800 bytes.
SYSTEM_TIME requires matching generated row-begin/end columns; system-period data versioning/history is established separately and is not implied by CREATE TABLE alone.
BUSINESS_TIME columns must be matching DATE or TIMESTAMP(6) WITHOUT TIME ZONE, NOT NULL, and application-maintained; Db2 adds the corresponding order check.
LOGGED/NOT LOGGED, COMPRESS, DSSIZE, BUFFERPOOL, MEMBER CLUSTER, TRACKMOD, and PAGENUM on CREATE TABLE are legal only for an implicitly created base table space, not an explicit target.
IN table-space, IN DATABASE, and IN ACCELERATOR are mutually exclusive placement alternatives.
PARTITION BY SIZE and PARTITION BY RANGE are mutually exclusive partitioning alternatives.
DSSIZE on CREATE TABLE must not be combined with the EVERY size in PARTITION BY SIZE.
PAGENUM RELATIVE is allowed only when a partitioning clause is specified; for current implicit CREATE TABLE usage this is the PBR path.
Implicit creation with no partition clause or PARTITION BY SIZE yields PBG; PARTITION BY RANGE yields PBR.
Every physical PBR table-space partition requires a range element and boundaries must progress in key order.
The last ending boundary is enforced; values beyond it are out of range, and mixed ASC/DESC/null/extrema behavior must be tested from the documented comparison rules.
LOB data requires ROWID plus a LOB table space, auxiliary table, and auxiliary index for each applicable LOB/partition; eligible implicit creation can supply them.
The first XML column causes an implicit document-ID column and implicit XML storage objects; validate those dependencies, not just the base table row.
DATA CAPTURE CHANGES conflicts with NOT LOGGED.

IN ACCELERATOR requires explicit column definitions and cannot use LIKE, AS-result, or MQT. It rejects the documented generated/default, column-attribute, constraint/period, partition, procedure, and physical/table options; CCSID has additional accelerator encoding restrictions. Unsupported types include DECFLOAT, LOB, ROWID, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, and XML.
Creating new hash-organized tables is unsupported at APPLCOMPAT V12R1M504 or later; keep grammar only for explicitly lower-compatibility regression cases.

Partition HASH SPACE requires ORGANIZE BY HASH UNIQUE and otherwise inherits the organization-level value. Hash organization conflicts with APPEND YES, IN ACCELERATOR, MEMBER CLUSTER, and basic row format; an explicitly placed PBR hash table cannot use PAGENUM RELATIVE.

Accepted compatibility spellings include NOCACHE, NOCYCLE, NOMINVALUE, NOMAXVALUE, NOORDER, PART plus VALUES, VALUES for ENDING AT, DEFINITION ONLY, CREATE SUMMARY TABLE, and TIMEZONE; preserve them in parse tests but emit current syntax in new templates.
Compare SYSTABLES, every SYSCOLUMNS row, constraint/relation rows, and enforcing/supporting indexes; parent-only comparison is incomplete.

clauses.summary: Controls index partition data-set size for PBR RPN only.

clauses.values: documented powers of two through 256 G, constrained by base table-space size
clauses.summary: Sets maximum data-set piece size for a nonpartitioned index.

clauses.values: NO or YES
clauses.summary: Enables image-copy and RECOVER support for an eligible index.

rules.text: An index supports at most 64 key/included columns under the form-specific counting rules; duplicates are prohibited.
Use IBM's separate padded/not-padded and partitioning/nonpartitioning formulas; partitioning keys are capped near 255 bytes and other keys near 2000 after nullable/varying/DECFLOAT overhead.
Expression keys use the restricted deterministic scalar grammar, cannot combine with INCLUDE/XML, and cannot specify DESC; execute against populated data to expose evaluation failures.
XML indexes use the specialized key-generation grammar and cannot be clustered, partitioned, padded, or combined with ordinary ordering/expression/INCLUDE forms as documented.
Ordinary UNIQUE treats null values as equal; UNIQUE WHERE NOT NULL permits multiple null-bearing keys but cannot enforce a table key constraint.
INCLUDE is limited to eligible unique ordinary indexes and rejects nonunique, expression/extended, XML, auxiliary, and other prohibited forms.
WITHOUT OVERLAPS supports temporal primary/unique enforcement; WITH OVERLAPS supports the temporal foreign-key side and cannot be UNIQUE.
PARTITION BY RANGE index-attribute blocks cannot be specified for an index defined with BUSINESS_TIME WITHOUT OVERLAPS.

A partitioning index is identified when its leading key matches the table partitioning columns/order/direction; PARTITIONED only requests physical alignment. A nonmatching PARTITIONED index is a DPSI; omission gives an NPI.
PARTITIONED is not supported for an index on a PBG table.
A unique physically partitioned index must contain the table partitioning columns in its key; INCLUDE does not satisfy that requirement.
EXCLUDE NULL KEYS conflicts with UNIQUE, BUSINESS_TIME WITHOUT OVERLAPS, XML, expression keys, INCLUDE, and a key set that cannot be all null.
PADDED is prohibited for VARBINARY and XML; with no varying key the option is ignored with padded physical behavior.
Index-partition attributes override index-level values, which override database/default values; the clause does not change table data boundaries.
COMPRESS YES requires an 8 KB, 16 KB, or 32 KB index buffer pool.
Index DSSIZE is valid only for an index on a PBR table space with relative page numbering.
PIECESIZE applies to a nonpartitioned index and is bounded by the base table-space size attributes.
DEFER YES leaves an eligible index on a populated table rebuild-pending; an empty-table index is not put into that state.
Primary/unique/eligible ROWID enforcement needs an ordinary UNIQUE index with the documented matching key; UNIQUE WHERE NOT NULL is insufficient.
Compare SYSINDEXES, every SYSINDEXPART row, SYSKEYS for ordinary keys, and SYSKEYTARGETS for expression/XML targets.

rules.text: LANGUAGE SQL without FENCED or EXTERNAL creates a native SQL procedure; a host-language external definition maps to a separately prepared program; LANGUAGE SQL with FENCED or EXTERNAL selects the deprecated external SQL form.
For native and current external procedures, SPECIFIC must repeat the procedure name. An explicit schema must match the procedure schema; an omitted schema inherits it.

ATOMIC cannot be specified on a compound statement in an SQL procedure. Use BEGIN or BEGIN NOT ATOMIC; internal statements retain their semicolons and the outermost statement has no embedded terminator.

External SQL procedures are deprecated and less fully supported than native SQL procedures; their CREATE statement must be processed through JCL or DSNTPSMP, so retain them only as compatibility cases.
All character and graphic parameters use one encoding scheme; per-parameter CCSID values and PARAMETER CCSID must agree.

PARAMETER VARCHAR is valid for a current external procedure only with LANGUAGE C and is also present in the deprecated external SQL procedure grammar. It excludes fixed strings, VARCHAR FOR BIT DATA, CLOB, DBCLOB, and implicitly generated parameters.
NO SQL is an external-procedure data-access option and is not part of the native SQL procedure grammar.
Scalar AS LOCATOR applies only to LOB values or distinct types based on LOBs and cannot be specified for an SQL procedure.
A TABLE LIKE ... AS LOCATOR parameter represents a transition table and the procedure can be invoked only from a trigger action; the captured row shape must match at invocation.
Whole-definition OR REPLACE preserves granted procedure privileges but discards the comment and reapplies system defaults for omitted options instead of retaining the old explicit values.

Native versions can change parameter names, options, and body, but cannot change parameter count, mode, type, character attributes, or CCSID; a table parameter prevents add/replace-version processing.
AUTONOMOUS must be specified for every version of a native procedure or for none of its versions.
A native SQL routine body is one SQL statement; multiple nested statements require one SQL control statement such as a compound block, and the nested rows come from SQL-procedure-statement.
Db2 checks local body statements and locally invoked routines against the declared data-access level; READS excludes modification and CONTAINS excludes both reading and modification.
Nested statements use semicolons but the outermost control statement does not; configure SPUFI, DSNTEP2, or similar processors with a distinct outer terminator to avoid truncating CREATE PROCEDURE.
Db2 implicitly binds a package whose collection/name/version are procedure schema/name/version; SYSPACKAGE.TYPE is N, and APPLCOMPAT plus other body bind options are verified on that package.
CONNECT, eligible remote three-part references, SET CURRENT PACKAGESET, or SET CURRENT PACKAGE PATH can require explicit copies of a native procedure package.
A routine or trigger cannot invoke a procedure defined with COMMIT ON RETURN YES; returned result-set cursors must be WITH HOLD to remain usable after a successful return commit.
AUTONOMOUS requires DYNAMIC RESULT SETS 0, excludes the documented LOB/XML-related parameter forms, cannot assign global variables, and cannot invoke another autonomous procedure.

Java requires EXTERNAL NAME and PARAMETER STYLE JAVA and prohibits DBINFO, PROGRAM TYPE MAIN, and RUN OPTIONS; REXX uses GENERAL or GENERAL WITH NULLS and permits only one OUT/INOUT parameter in the last position; DBINFO requires PARAMETER STYLE SQL.

Successful catalog registration does not prove that the external executable, package, WLM environment, Language Environment setup, and external-security authorization will succeed on first invocation.
For a native procedure, WLM ENVIRONMENT is valid only as WLM ENVIRONMENT FOR DEBUG MODE; DISABLE DEBUG MODE cannot later be relaxed for that version and causes the debug WLM value to be ignored.
Referencing global variables requires at least CONTAINS SQL, modifying them requires MODIFIES SQL DATA, and an autonomous procedure cannot assign a global variable.
WRAPPED cannot be used on a static CREATE statement or on a CREATE statement that adds or replaces a version of an existing native procedure.

Compare SYSROUTINES definition/version/options/text, ordered SYSPARMS rows, native SYSPACKAGE TYPE N and SYSPACKDEP DTYPE N rows, and SYSROUTINEAUTH grants when authorization is in scope; test external first-call readiness separately.

rules.text: MODE DB2SQL is required for a basic trigger and must be absent for an advanced trigger; SYSTRIGGERS.SQLPL is blank for basic and Y for advanced.
A basic BEFORE trigger must spell its activation time NO CASCADE BEFORE; bare BEFORE is valid only in the advanced trigger grammar.
Advanced triggers require application compatibility V12R1M500 or higher; the advanced APPLCOMPAT option also accepts only V12R1M500 or higher.
BEFORE and AFTER require an eligible base table; INSTEAD OF requires an eligible view and only one INSTEAD OF trigger is allowed for each operation on that view.

A BEFORE or AFTER subject must be an existing local base table, not a materialized query table, clone, temporary table, auxiliary table, alias, synonym, real-time statistics table, accelerator-only table, catalog table, or directory table.

An INSTEAD OF subject must be an eligible local view: symmetric-view relationships, mixed encoding/CCSID, ROWID or restricted underlying column types, field procedures, disallowed all-catalog/all-DGTT/all-clone bases, and dependent views make it ineligible under the documented view restrictions.
FOR EACH STATEMENT is valid only for AFTER; BEFORE and INSTEAD OF require FOR EACH ROW.
UPDATE OF column-name cannot be specified for an INSTEAD OF trigger; every listed column must belong to the subject table and appear once.

OLD is available for DELETE/UPDATE; NEW for INSERT/UPDATE. BEFORE row triggers allow variables but no transition tables; AFTER/INSTEAD OF row triggers allow matching variables and tables; AFTER statement triggers allow matching tables but no variables.
The optional ROW keyword after OLD or NEW belongs only to the advanced trigger grammar; a basic trigger must use OLD [AS] name or NEW [AS] name.
At most one OLD, NEW, OLD_TABLE, and NEW_TABLE declaration is allowed, and every correlation name and table identifier in REFERENCING must be unique from every other one.
Transition tables are read-only. Only NEW transition variables in BEFORE INSERT or BEFORE UPDATE can be assigned; AFTER and INSTEAD OF transition variables cannot be modified.
An XML transition variable or an XML column of a transition table cannot be referenced by an SQL-procedure-statement in a trigger body.
WHEN cannot be specified for an INSTEAD OF trigger; a BEFORE trigger condition fullselect cannot reference the subject table.
A basic body contains only the 12 documented statement families, with activation-time restrictions recorded in db2z13-trigger-body-statements.json; BEGIN ATOMIC only sequences that same closed set.

An advanced body is one direct triggered statement or one SQL control statement. Multiple statements require a control statement such as a compound block, whose nested statements come from the 35 trigger-supported SQL-procedure-statement rows.

Within an SQL PL control statement, advanced triggers allow CREATE TABLE at any activation time (without LOB or XML columns), and CREATE INDEX or CREATE VIEW only for AFTER/INSTEAD OF. CREATE STOGROUP, DATABASE, and TABLESPACE are excluded matrix rows; CREATE TRIGGER is absent from the SQL-procedure-statement grammar.

A BEFORE body cannot contain DELETE, INSERT, MERGE, REFRESH TABLE, TRUNCATE, UPDATE, or SELECT FROM a data-change statement, and cannot directly or indirectly invoke a routine containing the broader side-effect list documented by CREATE TRIGGER.

Body statements cannot use host variables or undefined transition variables, cannot reference declared temporary tables, and can directly reference only current-server tables, views, routines, and functions; referenced objects must exist when the definition is created.
A basic trigger body statement must not reference a parameter marker.
A table-locator-reference element must not be specified in a trigger body, although a transition table can be passed to a routine with TABLE before its table identifier as documented.
CREATE TRIGGER and ALTER TRIGGER statements cannot contain a hexadecimal graphic string (GX) constant.

A trigger cannot directly or indirectly call a procedure that issues COMMIT, CONNECT, RELEASE connection, RELEASE SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK without TO SAVEPOINT, SAVEPOINT, or SET CONNECTION, and cannot call a procedure defined COMMIT ON RETURN.
A trigger body statement must not modify a column that is part of a BUSINESS_TIME period.

The outermost compound statement of an advanced trigger defaults to ATOMIC and cannot specify NOT ATOMIC; nested compound statements default to NOT ATOMIC, and ATOMIC cannot be nested inside an ATOMIC compound.
RETURN appears in the SQL-control-statement overview but its statement-specific restriction prohibits RETURN in every trigger.
SECURED is mandatory when row or column access control applies to the subject table, or to an underlying table of the subject view.
The user who issues the activating DML does not need authority to execute the trigger body; the body executes with the authority of the trigger owner.
WRAPPED obfuscated statement text can be executed only for a dynamic CREATE TRIGGER statement; WRAPPED is prohibited on a static CREATE statement.
All versions share activation time, event, subject table/view, and granularity; REFERENCING content and body/options can differ by version.

Definition processing uses CURRENT APPLICATION COMPATIBILITY and is recorded through SYSTRIGGERS.ENVID to SYSENVIRONMENT.APPLCOMPAT; body SQL uses the trigger APPLCOMPAT option and is recorded in SYSPACKAGE.APPLCOMPAT.
The trigger schema/name becomes the package collection/name; SYSPACKAGE.TYPE is T for a basic trigger package and 1 for an advanced trigger package.
Only AFTER triggers cascade to deeper levels; Db2 permits 16 nested trigger/routine/function levels and rejects the 17th, backing out Db2 changes in the chain.

Db2 runs all BEFORE triggers before AFTER triggers. Within the same subject/event/time, creation timestamp determines order; for two row triggers, the earlier trigger processes every affected row before the next trigger starts. Dropping/recreating or whole-trigger OR REPLACE can move a trigger later.
SPUFI, the Db2 command line processor, and DSNTEP2 can truncate CREATE TRIGGER at embedded semicolons when semicolon is the outer terminator; use a different outer SQL terminator for compound bodies.
CREATE TRIGGER is not allowed on a table with pending definition changes.

Compare SYSTRIGGERS definition/version/type/text, SYSPACKAGE package attributes, SYSPACKDEP dependencies, and SYSENVIRONMENT definition APPLCOMPAT; compare CREATEDTS separately when activation order is under test.
